words.prose: {{ar:سَنُقْرِئُكَ}} ({{tr:sanuqriʾuka}}) opens the ayah as a complete one-word promise: future prefix, first-person plural divine subject, Form IV causation, and second-person object are all compressed before the result clause arrives. The addressee is not commanded to produce recitation from himself; he is made the recipient and performer of a recitation enabled by the speaker. The unspoken content after the verb is the same domain later protected from forgetting, so reception and retention are bound by shared ellipsis rather than by repeated nouns. The {{ar:ق ر ء}} ({{tr:q-r-ʾ}}) range keeps recitation as ordered, gathered articulation, while local grammar selects causative recitation and not unrelated cycle or womb branches. After the third-person divine acts and pasture-to-residue scene (87:1-5), this direct address turns ecological completion into projected verbal preservation, personalizing the gathering-and-recitation responsibility of 75:17-18 and shifting the familiar command {{ar:ٱقْرَأْ}} ({{tr:iqraʾ}}) (96:1) into enabled reception before 87:7 keeps the promise under divine will. The dense {{ar:ق ر ء}} ({{tr:q-r-ʾ}}) articulation makes the promised delivery feel controlled before the ayah opens into the denied loss.

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is the hinge where caused recitation becomes protected memory. It does not merely attach to the following negator as spelling; it links the whole {{ar:لَا تَنسَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:lā tansā}}) outcome to {{ar:سَنُقْرِئُكَ}} ({{tr:sanuqriʾuka}}). That makes non-forgetting consequential rather than a loosely coordinated second favor, while the particle's close-sequence value keeps the result immediate. Even though the written surface fuses into {{ar:فَلَا}} ({{tr:fa-lā}}), the analytic split preserves the particle's independent scope over the clause transition. Its short sound runs directly into the negation, so the listener meets denial of forgetting already attached to the promise.

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) negates {{ar:تَنسَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tansā}}), not the promise that precedes it. The clause is therefore promissory, not an imperative command to remember: the expected lapse is denied as the result of being made to recite. The reported {{ar:لَنْ}} ({{tr:lan}}) reading sharpens future denial and shows that the negation slot after {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) is structurally real, but the source surface remains broad {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) with the imperfect. That broad denial blocks not just one remembered episode but the operative vulnerability of future forgetting, yet it is bounded because 87:7 immediately qualifies it with a divine-will exception. The open vowel of {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) also carries into the long close of {{ar:تَنسَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tansā}}), making the negation and the denied verb sound joined.

words.prose: {{ar:تَنسَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tansā}}) names the vulnerability at the ayah's close and places it under negation. Its hidden 2ms subject is the same addressee marked by the {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) suffix in {{ar:سَنُقْرِئُكَ}} ({{tr:sanuqriʾuka}}): the recipient of caused recitation becomes the protected rememberer. The verb remains semantically transitive but objectless, so the listener must carry the recited content forward as what will not be forgotten or neglected. The {{ar:ن س ي}} ({{tr:n-s-y}}) range includes mental lapse, neglect, and abandoned cast-off things; local context narrows that range to loss or neglect of the caused recitation, not sciatic, postponement, or other remote branches. The simple Form I names ordinary human lapse rather than caused or feigned forgetting, and {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) suspends that process without changing the stem. Ending on this denied verb makes the promise land on the exact threat it cancels, while 87:7 immediately keeps any exception under divine will; set beside 19:64's denial of divine forgetfulness and Adam's forgetting in 20:115, this recitation is protected from paradigmatic human lapse without making the addressee's retention autonomous. The long final {{ar:ىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ā}}) lets the threatened loss linger audibly as suspended non-loss.

topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:تَنسَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tansā}}) as having an unexpressed 2ms subject matching the addressed object in {{ar:سَنُقْرِئُكَ}} ({{tr:sanuqriʾuka}}).

topics.reason: The verb instance is marked obj=none_absolute with a transfer warning that Arabic does not express an object; the prior recitation clause supplies the recoverable domain.

topics.headline: future lapse prevented
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the root shifted from reported forgetting into a prevented future or ongoing lapse at the ayah's close.
topics.reason: QAC marks a 2ms imperfect negated by {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}); the profile notes frequent negated/scoped uses for this exact root-form group.

topics.headline: forgetting and neglect range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promise protects both recall and faithful attention to the recited content, while the local object-domain limits the broad root range.
topics.reason: V4 supports forgetting, neglect, and abandoned-thing branches for {{ar:ن س ي}} ({{tr:n-s-y}}), but local syntax selects loss or neglect of the prior recited content rather than remote branches.

topics.headline: ordinary lapse, not caused or feigned
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees ordinary human forgetting named directly, while causative or feigned-forgetting forms remain only contrastive background.
topics.reason: The surface is simple Form I {{ar:تَنسَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tansā}}), so causative {{ar:نَسَّى}} ({{tr:nassā}}), {{ar:أَنْسَى}} ({{tr:ansā}}), and feigned {{ar:تَنَاسَى}} ({{tr:tanāsā}}) are valid contrasts but not the local stem.

topics.headline: human weakness suspended
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices protection from a paradigmatic human weakness, without importing a different root or making the addressee's retention autonomous.
topics.reason: Rows cite divine non-forgetfulness in 19:64 and Adam's forgetting in 20:115; the local root remains {{ar:ن س ي}} ({{tr:n-s-y}}), so the human-forgetfulness dispute is retained as pressure, not as a replacement root.

topics.headline: closure opens to exception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final word is exactly the domain qualified by 87:7, so the assurance stays under divine will.
topics.reason: The next ayah's exception in 87:7 qualifies the non-forgetting claim anchored in the final verb of 87:6.

topics.headline: long final suspended loss

topics.reason: The phonetic rows concern the actual final shape of {{ar:تَنسَىٰٓ}} ({{tr:tansā}}) and its relation to the preceding negation and earlier recitation articulation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Recitation as ordered gathering against loss.** Lexical evidence: ق ر ء B001/B002 (gathering speech into recitation; teaching recitation), ن س ي B001 (loss of recall). Structural cue: 87:5's disordered refuse precedes 87:6's gathered speech. Assigned role: نقرئك gathers the discourse into a repeatable whole; فلا تنسى blocks its decay. Abductive move: memory is preserved when speech is structured as recitation. Reading change: the promise is active formation of durable order, not merely a forecast that forgetting will not occur.

2. **Protection from becoming a cast-off thing.** Lexical evidence: ن س ي B003 (forgotten discarded low-value thing), غ ث و B004 in 87:5 (unregarded refuse), ب ق ي B001 in 87:17 (persistence). Structural cue: the chaff image sits immediately before the anti-forgetting promise. Assigned role: نسيان threatens to turn revelation into abandoned residue; recitation keeps it from that status. Abductive move: cognitive abandonment and material refuse are structurally analogous. Reading change: "you will not forget" becomes preservation from degradation.

3. **Teaching as preparation for public reminder.** Lexical evidence: ق ر ء B002/B006 (reading/teaching; devout reader), ذ ك ر B004/B009 in 87:9 and ذ ك ر B004 in 87:15. Structural cue: "We will make you recite" precedes "so remind." Assigned role: divine recitation installs the material that can later be made public as reminder. Abductive move: one cannot remind beneficially unless first made a reliable bearer. Reading change: 87:6 becomes an authorization and training scene.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 87:18-19 made recitation feel archival as well as oral: the promise not to forget aligns with صحف as preserved written sheets. 87:5 was the strongest backward surprise, turning forgetting into a chaff/refuse danger.

reader_b.activated_readings_md:
1. **Recitation as gathered speech secured against loss.** Lexical evidence: قرء B001 gathering speech into recitation and B002 reading/teaching recitation; نسي B001 forgetting/loss of recall. Structural cue: future divine "we will make you recite" followed by "so you do not forget." Assigned role: قرء gathers the material; نسي names the failure being blocked. Abductive move: the packet supplies gathering and forgetting; I infer that divine recitation creates retention. Reading change: the ayah reads as a preservation mechanism, not only a promise of delivery.

2. **Womb-like retention of revelation.** Lexical evidence: قرء B003 womb gathering/bearing and B004 womb enclosing pregnancy; رحم B003 womb in 87:0; خلق B002 originating in 87:2. Structural cue: the opening mercy/womb field precedes "we will make you recite." Assigned role: the addressee's memory becomes a vessel that encloses what is being brought forth. Abductive move: the packet supplies womb branches for both رحم and قرء; I infer an analogy between gestation and retained recitation. Reading change: revelation is carried until uttered, not simply heard and repeated.

3. **Against abandonment, not just mental lapse.** Lexical evidence: نسي B002 leaving/abandoning a covenant or command; رعي B006 preserving a claim; ذكر B009 reminder/admonition in 87:9. Structural cue: reminder follows the anti-forgetting promise. Assigned role: "forgetting" can mean neglect of an entrusted obligation. Abductive move: the packet gives abandonment and later reminder; I infer that preservation is ethical as well as cognitive. Reading change: "you will not forget" becomes "you will not be left to abandon the entrusted recitation."

4. **Teaching by collected cycles.** Lexical evidence: قرء B002 appointed time/cycle and B005 appointed time arriving; قدر B001 measured term; يسر B001 ease in 87:8. Structural cue: divine instruction is followed by divine easing. Assigned role: recitation unfolds in timed, measured pedagogy. Abductive move: the packet supplies cycle/time and measure; I infer paced instruction. Reading change: the promise becomes an ordered curriculum rather than a single transfer.
reader_b.retrospective_surprises_md: 87:9-10 made this ayah less private: the preserved recitation exists so reminder can happen and the fearful can remember. 87:18-19 made retention look like a living counterpart to written sheets: oral preservation and archival صحف mirror each other.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Recitation is gathered speech made retainable.** The “gathering speech into recitation” variant of `ق ر ء/B001` anchors `سَنُقْرِئُكَ`, and `ن س ي/B001` supplies loss of recall. The causative first-person verb followed by `فَلَا` gives a production-to-retention sequence; later `ذ ك ر` repetition in 87:9–10 confirms recall as the receiving mechanism. Recitation’s role is to assemble discourse into a whole, while the negation protects that whole from dispersal. I infer that gathering enables retention. The ayah reads as formation of durable verbal memory, not only an instruction to read.
2. **The negation also excludes abandonment.** `ن س ي/B002` is leaving or neglecting, not merely involuntary forgetting. The window places discarded `غُثَاء` behind the clause and active `يَتَجَنَّبُهَا` in 87:11 ahead of it. Those two forms distinguish being cast off, being preserved, and deliberately moving aside. The branch assigns `فَلَا تَنسَىٰ` covenantal or practical continuity: the recited matter will not be left unused. I infer agency-sensitive contrast from the sequence. The reading changes from memory assurance alone to protection against neglect.
3. **The future can be heard as staged recurrence.** The appointed-time or cycle variant of `ق ر ء/B005` is activated by the future prefix `سـ`, by the earlier measured lifecycle, and by repeated reminder in 87:9–10. Its role is to distribute recitation through successive occasions rather than compress it into one event. I infer periodic delivery from those cues; the form itself primarily supports causative recitation, so this reading is exploratory. On this reading, non-forgetting is continuity across renewed episodes of reception.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 87:9–10 confirmed that the gathered recitation does not stop with the addressee but becomes reminder and recollection in another. 87:11 then corrected `فَلَا تَنسَىٰ` from a purely cognitive promise: its `ن س ي/B002` abandonment sense stands against another person’s active decision to move the reminder aside.

findings.text: Okutma, sözleri dağılmayacak bir bütün halinde toplayıp hafızada tutan bir koruma düzenine dönüşür.
Unutmama vaadi, yalnız zihinsel kaybı değil, emanet edilen sözü terk edip işlemez bırakmayı da dışlar.
Toplanan okuma, son ayetlerdeki yazılı sayfaların sözlü koruma karşılığı olarak belirir.
Okunan söz, rahimde taşınan bir şey gibi içeride tutulup zamanı geldiğinde dışarı çıkarılan emanet olarak da düşünülebilir.
Okutma, tek seferlik aktarım yerine ölçülü zamanlarda yenilenen bir öğretim döngüsü olarak da okunabilir.

butuncul_okuma_line.raw_line: **87:6.** “Sana okutacağız, unutmayacaksın” ayetinin birincil okuması, vahyin Peygamber’e öğretilip korunacağıdır. İkincil okuma ise “okutma”yı toplayıp bir bütün hâline getirme, “unutmama”yı da yalnız zihinsel hatırlama değil emaneti terk etmeme olarak gösterir. Daha şaşırtıcı katmanda, قرء kökünün rahim ve taşıma çağrışımları, vahyin hafızada doğuma hazırlanan korunmuş bir emanet gibi taşındığını düşündürür. {ق ر ء:B001,B002,B003,B004,B005; ن س ي:B001,B002; ر ح م:B003; ذ ك ر:B009}
